text:
tess: hey all, day 2 and running into weird networking. From WSL2 my dev server can't reach internal kibana (kibana.internal:5601) or the internal package registry (packages.internal). curl to kibana.ip returns "connection refused" but `ping` from Windows powershell resolves to 10.60.5.11. I'm on company WireGuard profile on my Windows laptop. Any known WSL quirks?

kevin: welcome @tess! WSL2 uses a virtualized network interface and sometimes the host->WSL routing plus split-tunnel gets messy. Quick Q: can you `wsl -d docker-desktop ip route` and post output?

tess: pasted route output: default via 172.22.224.1 dev eth0 proto dhcp metric 202
10.60.0.0/16 via 172.22.0.1 dev eth0 proto static metric 50

jules: looks like the default route metric in WSL is higher than the host's, so traffic to 10.60.0.0/16 might be hitting the Windows stack which then tries to use the public NIC instead of the WireGuard adapter. On Windows we prefer adding a persistent route for the internal ranges with the WG adapter gateway or altering metric.

tess: how do I do that safely? i'm on a company laptop (managed).

mario: two quick approaches: 1) add a host-level static route via elevated powershell: `New-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix 10.60.0.0/16 -InterfaceAlias "WireGuard" -NextHop 0.0.0.0 -RouteMetric 10` (your interface alias might differ). 2) enable WSL to use the host's DNS and routing by updating `wsl.conf` and restarting: set `networking.generateResolvConf = false` then copy resolv.conf. Both need admin.

tess: i don't have admin. Is there a non-admin workaround?

jules: yes: use the bastion SOCKS proxy from WSL. `ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa -J jump@bastion.redwood.net -D 1080 -N user@localhost` from WSL or from Windows powershell. Then in WSL set `all_proxy=socks5h://localhost:1080` for your tools, or `curl -x socks5h://localhost:1080 http://kibana.internal:5601`. It routes through the bastion so bypasses host route problems.

tess: tried SOCKS from WSL, kibana loads! But docker inside WSL still can't pull from packages.internal:5000 (hangs).

kevin: for docker you can forward a local port: from Windows run `ssh -L 127.0.0.1:5000:packages.internal:5000 -J jump@bastion.redwood.net -N -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa` then in WSL point docker to 127.0.0.1:5000. Alternatively, use `socat` inside WSL to forward via SOCKS, but that's gnarly.

infra-bot: Ticket INF-9123 opened by tess: "WSL2 routing to internal subnets broken under split-tunnel" Assigned: kevin ETA: 6h

mario: long-term infra note: we should add a checklist step for Windows+WSL tokens: if device is managed and you need heavy internal access, request the "full-tunnel-onboard" tag during asset provisioning. That will avoid WSL host routing problems. Also we'll add a devex doc with the ssh-forward and docker workaround.

tess: thanks everyone, SOCKS + port forward saved my afternoon. i'll confirm with IT for the full-tunnel tag. :grin:

kevin: actionable: a) eng-infra to add WSL troubleshooting doc and port-forward snippets (kevin) b) devex to include WSL note in new-hire checklist (jules) c) tess to request full-tunnel tag if needed (tess)
